title: PRINCE2 Practitioner
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus (application of principles, themes, and processes to scenarios). Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A competitor has launched a service that removes the expected benefits from a project, and the latest business case forecast is now clearly negative. What is the MOST appropriate action for the project board to take?
options: Recommend that the project be stopped because it no longer has continued business justification
Continue the project so the money already spent is not wasted
Ask the project manager to delay reporting the finding until the next stage boundary
Cut the scope until the forecast looks positive again
items.explanation: Continued business justification is a PRINCE2 principle and requires a valid Business Case throughout. When the forecast benefits disappear the board should stop or redirect the project rather than continue for sunk-cost reasons or conceal the position.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: A project manager is about to start a project that closely resembles one completed last year, and wants to benefit from the earlier team's hindsight. Which action BEST applies the learn from experience principle?
options: Rely on individual team members to remember previous problems informally
Record and review lessons from the earlier project in the Lessons Log when planning new work
Ignore the earlier project because every project is unique
Wait until this project closes and then collect lessons for future projects
items.explanation: Learn from experience means lessons are sought, recorded, and acted on throughout the project, so reviewing the earlier project's Lessons Log at planning time is the correct application. Ignoring or delaying lessons loses their value and relying on memory is unreliable.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: Two directors both insist on acting as the project's Executive, and decisions are being delayed while they disagree. Which action BEST applies the defined roles and responsibilities principle?
options: Give the project manager final decision-making authority instead
Create a separate steering committee to break any deadlock
Appoint a single Executive and let the project board represent business, user, and supplier interests
Allow both directors to share the Executive role equally
items.explanation: PRINCE2 requires one Executive who is ultimately accountable, supported by the project board's three stakeholder interests. Shared or absent accountability causes ambiguity, and moving decisions to the project manager or a new committee does not fix the role conflict.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: A two-year project has high uncertainty about requirements that will not be clarified until later. How should the project manager apply the manage by stages principle?
options: Plan the entire two years in detail before initiation is authorized
Avoid stage boundaries so the team can keep changing direction freely
Use one stage for the whole project to keep governance overhead low
Divide the project into management stages with a decision review at each stage boundary
items.explanation: Manage by stages breaks the project into manageable chunks so the board can review progress, the business case, and risk at each boundary. Full upfront planning or a single stage removes the control points that make this principle effective.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: The project manager forecasts that the current stage will exceed its agreed cost tolerance but does not tell the project board. Which PRINCE2 principle has the project manager failed to apply?
options: Manage by exception, because tolerances are delegated and the board must be told when they are forecast to be exceeded
Focus on products, because the stage products were not defined
Learn from experience, because the overspend was not recorded
Tailor to suit the project environment, because the controls were not adapted
items.explanation: Manage by exception sets tolerances at each level and requires escalation to the next level when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded. Reporting only after the event denies the board the chance to direct, and the other principles are not the issue here.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: Team members are arguing about what a key deliverable should contain and when it will be finished. Which action BEST applies the focus on products principle?
options: Focus on the activity schedule and let the product emerge from the tasks
Agree a Product Description with quality criteria and acceptance criteria before planning the work
Start building the deliverable and define its contents once work is under way
Let the team manager decide the contents without documenting them
items.explanation: Focus on products means defining and agreeing products, their quality criteria, and acceptance criteria before planning activities. Starting work first or leaving the definition implicit leads to the disagreement the project is experiencing.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: A small, low-risk internal project is being buried in the same volume of documentation that a large programme would use. What should the project manager do while applying the tailor to suit principle?
options: Abandon PRINCE2 entirely because the project is too small
Keep the documentation as it is to make the project look well managed
Adapt the themes, processes, roles, and products to the project's scale, complexity, and risk while retaining the principles
Apply every PRINCE2 product and process at full weight because the method says so
items.explanation: Tailor to suit the project environment means scaling the method to the project while always applying the seven principles. Applying everything at full weight or dropping the method ignores this principle, and retaining unnecessary documentation adds no value.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: At a stage boundary the project manager must confirm that the project still makes business sense. Which action BEST supports the continued business justification principle?
options: Assume the original Business Case is still valid because nothing has formally changed
Delegate the Business Case review to the team manager
Postpone the Business Case review until the project is closed
Review and update the Business Case with current benefits, costs, risks, and timescales for the board
items.explanation: Continued business justification requires the Business Case to be reviewed and updated at each stage boundary so the board can confirm it remains valid. Assuming it is unchanged, delegating it inappropriately, or deferring it to closure all remove that assurance.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: Midway through a stage a supplier's approach fails and the team discovers a much better method. What should the project manager do to apply the learn from experience principle?
options: Record the lesson in the Lessons Log immediately and share it so the current and other projects can benefit
Save the lesson until the end of the project so it is captured with all the others
Keep the lesson within the team to avoid distracting the rest of the project
Report it only in the End Project Report so it is formally documented
items.explanation: Learn from experience means lessons are captured and used as soon as they arise, not only at closure. Delaying, hoarding, or confining the lesson to closure documentation wastes the chance to improve current work and other projects.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: A requested change would exceed the change authority delegated to the project manager. Who should decide whether the change proceeds?
options: The project support officer who maintains the Issue Register
The project board acting as the change authority because the change exceeds the delegated limit
The project manager, because all changes are a project management matter
The team manager who owns the affected work package
items.explanation: Defined roles and responsibilities include clear change authority limits. A change beyond the project manager's limit must go to the project board, while the team manager and project support roles hold no such authority under PRINCE2.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Principles

items.stem: A project's Business Case is being prepared and the project manager asks who is ultimately accountable for it. Which role owns the Business Case in PRINCE2?
options: The Senior User, who represents the people using the product
The Senior Supplier, who provides the resources to build the product
The Executive, who is accountable for the project's continued business justification
The project manager, who writes and maintains the document
items.explanation: The Executive is accountable for the Business Case, although the project manager prepares and maintains it. The Senior User and Senior Supplier contribute their interests but do not own the Business Case.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: When developing the Business Case the team only considers building the full solution. What should the project manager ensure is also included?
options: Only the preferred option so the board is not confused
A single option based on the project manager's preference
Options for suppliers but not for the scope of the solution
Business options such as doing nothing, doing the minimum, and doing something, with their costs and benefits
items.explanation: PRINCE2 requires the Business Case to present business options so the investment decision is informed. Comparing the do-nothing and do-minimum options with the preferred option avoids a predetermined conclusion, while a single option does not support a real decision.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: Many of the project's benefits will only be measurable two years after the project closes. How should this be handled under the Business Case theme?
options: Document how and when benefits will be measured in the Benefits Review Plan
Ignore benefits that cannot be measured while the project is running
Claim the benefits at project closure based on forecasts alone
Leave benefit measurement to the finance department without a plan
items.explanation: The Benefits Review Plan records how and when the project's benefits will be measured, including after closure. Ignoring post-closure benefits, claiming them from forecasts, or leaving measurement unplanned fails the Business Case theme.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project board needs someone to represent the interests of the people who will use the final product and to specify their requirements. Which role should do this?
options: The project manager, who runs the project day to day
The Senior User, who represents user interests and specifies their requirements
The Senior Supplier, who represents the build side of the project
The Executive, who represents the business interest
items.explanation: The Senior User represents the users' interests and specifies their needs and benefits. The Senior Supplier represents those building the products, the Executive represents the business, and the project manager manages delivery rather than representing user interests.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project board wants independent monitoring of the project's quality, business, and user aspects without managing it. Which role provides this?
options: The team manager, who manages the delivery of products
Project Support, which provides administrative services
Project Assurance, which is an independent board responsibility that can be delegated to others
The project manager, who also reports progress to the board
items.explanation: Project Assurance monitors the project objectively on behalf of the board and is independent of the project manager. The project manager, team manager, and project support roles all have delivery or administrative duties, so none is independent.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A project is large enough that work is carried out by several separate teams, each needing day-to-day direction. Which role should the project manager appoint?
options: An extra Project Assurance role for each team
A deputy project manager to control every team
A change authority to coordinate the teams
A team manager for each team, taking direction from the project manager
items.explanation: The Team Manager role is used when one person cannot directly manage all the teams, and team managers take direction from the project manager. Project Assurance, deputy, and change authority roles address control and approval, not day-to-day team direction.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A project has many stakeholders with differing information needs, and reporting is ad hoc. What should the project manager produce to address this?
options: A Communication Management Approach describing the stakeholders and how the project will communicate with them
A Risk Management Approach because communication is uncertain
A Quality Register listing the required reviews
An End Stage Report summarizing communications to date
items.explanation: The Communication Management Approach identifies stakeholders and defines the means, frequency, and responsibilities for communicating with them. Risk, quality, and reporting products do not provide a stakeholder communication strategy.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A product review is planned and the project manager needs to appoint the roles needed by the PRINCE2 quality review technique. Which combination is required?
options: The team manager and any available team member
Chair, presenter, reviewers, and an approver, supported by an administrator
Only the author and the project manager
The Executive and the Senior Supplier alone
items.explanation: The PRINCE2 quality review technique uses a chair, presenter, reviewers, and approver, with an administrator supporting the process. The other combinations omit the separation of roles that makes the review objective.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A product has been built but the team cannot agree whether it is acceptable. What should have been defined in the Product Description to prevent this?
options: The activity list and duration estimating assumptions
The supplier's company registration details
The quality criteria and quality tolerance that determine acceptable and unacceptable results
The name of the developer who would build the product
items.explanation: A Product Description states the quality criteria and quality tolerance that make a product acceptable. Developer identity and supplier registration are irrelevant, and activity information belongs in plans rather than defining product acceptability.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project board wants to see all planned and completed quality activities and their results in one place. Which management product should the project manager maintain?
options: The Issue Register, which records issues and changes
The Risk Register, which records risks and responses
The Lessons Log, which records lessons for the project
The Quality Register, which records quality activities and their results
items.explanation: The Quality Register is where planned and performed quality activities, and their results, are recorded. The Issue, Risk, and Lessons products record different things and would not give the board this quality view.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project manager is drafting the Project Product Description and needs to record what the customer will consider a successful final product. Which content should be included?
options: The customer's quality expectations and the acceptance criteria for the final product
The project's resource rates and cost rates
The list of team members and their availability
The project's risk appetite statement
items.explanation: The Project Product Description captures the customer's quality expectations, the acceptance criteria, and the acceptance method. Rates, resources, and risk appetite belong in other management products and do not define customer acceptance.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A team manager needs a plan that covers only the work packages assigned to that team. Which type of plan should the team manager produce?
options: A Benefits Review Plan, which covers benefit measurement
A Team Plan, which covers the work packages assigned to the team
A Project Plan, which covers the whole project
An Exception Plan, which replaces a stage plan after a tolerance breach
items.explanation: A Team Plan is produced for a team's assigned work packages. The Project Plan covers the whole project, an Exception Plan responds to a tolerance breach, and the Benefits Review Plan addresses benefit measurement, so none is the right level here.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project manager begins planning by listing the activities needed to build a product. How should PRINCE2 product-based planning be applied instead?
options: Start with the team roster and allocate tasks alphabetically
Start with the risk register and build products to avoid risks
Start with a Product Breakdown Structure, then write Product Descriptions, then create a Product Flow Diagram
Start with a Gantt chart and derive products from the schedule
items.explanation: Product-based planning moves from a Product Breakdown Structure to Product Descriptions and then a Product Flow Diagram before activities are planned. Starting from a schedule, roster, or risk register inverts the method and weakens focus on products.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A stage is forecast to exceed its time tolerance and the board asks the project manager to recover. What should the project manager produce before the board can authorize recovery?
options: A new Project Brief replacing the original
A Checkpoint Report summarizing the last week
A revised Benefits Review Plan for post-closure benefits
An Exception Plan that covers the period from the point of the deviation to the end of the stage or project
items.explanation: When a tolerance is breached, an Exception Plan is produced to replace the stage or project plan for the remaining period and is approved by the board. The Project Brief, Checkpoint Report, and Benefits Review Plan do not provide the recovery plan the board needs.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A project relies on a single overseas supplier and the team decides to use a second supplier to reduce the chance of disruption. Which risk response is this?
options: Reduce, because the action decreases the probability or impact of the risk
Transfer, because the risk is moved to another party
Accept, because no action is taken
Exploit, because a positive opportunity is pursued
items.explanation: Using a second supplier lowers the probability or impact of supplier disruption, which is a reduce response. Transfer would move the risk to another party, accept would do nothing, and exploit applies to opportunities rather than threats.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A risk has been identified and a response agreed. Which responsibility should be assigned to the risk owner?
options: Auditing the project's risk management approach
Managing, monitoring, and controlling the specific risk, including triggering the response
Carrying out the response actions on behalf of the risk owner
Approving the project's risk appetite
items.explanation: The risk owner is responsible for managing, monitoring, and controlling a specific risk and for triggering its response. The person who performs the response actions is the risk actionee, while risk appetite and assurance are board-level matters.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: Two risks are being compared. Risk A has a 20 percent chance of a 100,000 cost impact and Risk B has an 80 percent chance of a 20,000 impact. What should the project manager conclude?
options: Both risks have the same expected value
Neither risk needs a response because the costs are estimates
Risk A has a higher expected value than Risk B, so it warrants greater attention
Risk B is more serious because its probability is higher
items.explanation: Expected value multiplies probability by impact, giving Risk A an expected value of 20,000 and Risk B of 16,000, so Risk A warrants more attention. Judging by probability alone or dismissing estimates misuses the assessment.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A project board wants a reserve set aside to fund specific risk responses. What should this reserve be called in PRINCE2?
options: A change budget, which pays for approved changes
A contingency plan, which is a course of action if a risk occurs
The project's capital expenditure line
A risk budget, which is money set aside to fund specific risk responses
items.explanation: The risk budget is the amount set aside to fund specific risk responses. The change budget funds approved changes, a contingency plan is a fallback course of action, and capital expenditure is unrelated to risk response funding.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: During a stage the supplier delivers a product that does not meet its Product Description. How should this be recorded in PRINCE2?
options: As an off-specification, because the product does not meet its agreed specification
As a request for change, because something about the product changed
As a concern, because the team is worried about the product
As a risk, because the product might fail later
items.explanation: An off-specification is an issue where a product will not meet a requirement or specification. A request for change proposes an alteration, a concern is a general matter, and a risk is a future uncertainty rather than a current shortfall.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project manager needs to know the current version and status of every configuration item. Which part of configuration management provides this?
options: Verification, which audits baselines against the items
Status accounting, which records and reports the status of configuration items
Identification, which names and versions items
Control, which approves changes to items
items.explanation: Status accounting records and reports the current status of configuration items. Identification names them, control manages changes to them, and verification audits that baselines contain the right items, so those activities do not answer the question.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A project has many changes and the board wants clarity on how changes will be assessed and who can approve them. Which management product should define this?
options: The Communication Management Approach, which covers stakeholder information
The Benefits Review Plan, which covers benefit measurement
The Change Control Approach, which defines how issues and changes are controlled and who decides
The Quality Register, which lists quality activities
items.explanation: The Change Control Approach sets out how issues and changes are identified, assessed, and decided, including change authority limits. The other products address quality, communication, and benefits and do not define change control.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project board wants to delegate authority to the project manager while retaining control. Which set of tolerances should the board agree for the project?
options: Only cost and time tolerances
Only scope and quality tolerances
Schedule tolerance only, because time is the main concern
Time, cost, quality, scope, benefit, and risk tolerances
items.explanation: PRINCE2 provides six tolerance areas, time, cost, quality, scope, benefit, and risk, so the board can delegate within limits while retaining control. Limiting tolerances to one or two areas would leave other dimensions uncontrolled.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project board wants regular progress information at a defined frequency during a stage. Which product should the project manager provide?
options: A Highlight Report, which the project manager sends to the board at agreed intervals
A Checkpoint Report, which the team manager sends to the project manager
An End Stage Report, which is produced at a stage boundary
An Exception Report, which is produced when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded
items.explanation: The Highlight Report is the time-driven progress report from the project manager to the board. Checkpoint Reports flow from team manager to project manager, End Stage Reports are event-driven at boundaries, and Exception Reports are triggered by tolerance deviations.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: The project manager forecasts that the stage will breach its tolerance on time. What should the project manager do FIRST?
options: Ask the team manager to resolve the deviation locally
Produce an Exception Report and escalate the forecast deviation to the project board
Wait until the stage ends and report the actual breach
Change the stage plan without telling the board
items.explanation: Under manage by exception, a forecast breach of tolerance triggers an Exception Report to the board so it can direct. Waiting for the breach, changing the plan unilaterally, or pushing the problem down all deny the board its control point.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Themes

items.stem: A project is triggered by a strategic initiative and the project manager is beginning the starting up a project process. What triggers this process?
options: An approved Exception Plan
An End Project Report
A project mandate, which provides the basis for initiating the project
A completed Project Initiation Documentation
items.explanation: The Starting up a Project process is triggered by the project mandate, which comes from corporate or programme management. A PID is produced later in Initiating a Project, while Exception Plans and End Project Reports belong to later stages or closure.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: At the start of the starting up a project process, which two roles should be appointed first?
options: The team manager and project support
The Senior User and the change authority
The project assurance and the project support officer
The Executive and the project manager
items.explanation: Starting up a Project begins by appointing the Executive and the project manager so the project can be initiated and the remaining roles designed. The other roles are appointed later as the project management team is established.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: During starting up a project the project manager needs an initial justification before full authorization. Which product provides this?
options: The outline Business Case within the Project Brief
The full Business Case within the Project Initiation Documentation
The Benefits Review Plan
The End Stage Report
items.explanation: Starting up a Project prepares an outline Business Case as part of the Project Brief. The full Business Case is developed and refined later in Initiating a Project, and the Benefits Review Plan and End Stage Report serve different purposes.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: What must the project manager do in starting up a project so the board can authorize initiation?
options: Close the project and evaluate the benefits
Plan the initiation stage and prepare the Project Brief for the board to authorize DP1
Complete the project plan and the PID before any authorization
Appoint all team managers and complete a work package
items.explanation: Starting up a Project ends by planning the initiation stage and assembling the Project Brief so the board can authorize initiation at Directing a Project activity DP1. Completing the PID belongs to initiation, and closing the project is a later process.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: Which role owns the directing a project process?
options: The team manager, who manages product delivery
Project support, which maintains the project's files
The project board, which is accountable for directing and taking key decisions
The project manager, who runs the project day to day
items.explanation: Directing a Project is owned by the project board, which remains accountable and makes the key authorization decisions. The project manager, team manager, and project support roles support or deliver rather than direct.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: The Project Brief and initiation stage plan are ready. Which activity lets the board commit resources to initiation?
options: Authorize the project, known as DP2
Authorize a stage or exception plan, known as DP3
Authorize project closure, known as DP5
Authorize initiation, known as DP1
items.explanation: Authorize initiation, DP1, is when the board approves the plan for and commitment to the initiation stage. DP2 authorizes the whole project after the PID, DP3 authorizes stages, and DP5 authorizes closure.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: The Project Initiation Documentation is complete. Which board activity authorizes the project to proceed?
options: Authorize the project, known as DP2, following review of the PID
Authorize initiation, known as DP1
Give ad hoc direction, known as DP4
Authorize project closure, known as DP5
items.explanation: Once the PID is assembled, the board authorizes the project at DP2. DP1 has already happened, DP4 covers ad hoc direction during the project, and DP5 relates to closure.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: During a stage a board member asks for an update on an emerging issue and gives guidance. Which directing a project activity is this?
options: Authorize project closure
Give ad hoc direction, which covers board involvement outside the formal decision points
Authorize initiation
Authorize a stage or exception plan
items.explanation: Give ad hoc direction covers board involvement and guidance between the formal authorization points. The other activities are specific decision points rather than ongoing direction during a stage.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: What is the main output of the initiating a project process?
options: The End Project Report, which closes the project
The Work Package, which assigns work to a team
The Project Initiation Documentation, which consolidates the detailed baseline for the project
The Project Brief, which started the project
items.explanation: Initiating a Project produces the Project Initiation Documentation, which brings together the project plan, business case, approaches, and controls. The Project Brief precedes it, while the End Project Report and Work Package belong to later processes.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: During initiation the project manager must decide how the project's risks, quality, changes, and communications will be managed. Which products should be prepared?
options: The Project Brief, the mandate, and the Daily Log
The End Stage Report and the Lessons Report
The Work Package and the Checkpoint Report
The Risk, Quality, Change Control, and Communication Management Approaches
items.explanation: Initiating a Project prepares the project's management approaches for risk, quality, change control, and communication. The Project Brief and mandate belong to starting up, and the other products belong to stage delivery or closure.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: During initiation the board wants to know how the project will be controlled and what tolerance it will delegate. Which activity covers this?
options: Set up the project controls, defining tolerances and the control mechanisms for the project
Authorize a work package for the team
Hand over the project's products to the customer
Evaluate the project's benefits against the business case
items.explanation: Setting up project controls during initiation establishes the project board's and project manager's tolerances and how the project will be monitored. Work package authorization, product handover, and benefit evaluation happen in later processes.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A project manager is refining the outline business case during initiation. Which action is appropriate?
options: Delegate responsibility for the Business Case to the team manager
Develop the full Business Case and include it in the Project Initiation Documentation for the board to authorize
Leave the outline Business Case as it is and proceed to delivery
Remove the Business Case from the PID to simplify the document
items.explanation: Initiating a Project refines the outline Business Case into a full Business Case within the PID for the board to authorize at DP2. Leaving the outline, removing it, or delegating ownership to the team manager fails the Business Case theme.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A stage is under way and the project manager needs to give the team manager authority to start a piece of work. Which action and product are appropriate?
options: Update the Project Brief with the new work
Request an Exception Plan from the team manager
Authorize a Work Package, agreeing its products, tolerances, and reporting requirements with the team manager
Produce an End Stage Report for the board
items.explanation: Controlling a Stage includes authorizing work packages, in which the project manager and team manager agree the work, products, tolerances, and reporting. End Stage Reports, Project Brief updates, and Exception Plans are used in other situations.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: During a stage the project manager wants regular progress updates from the team managers and must also report to the board. Which reports are used?
options: Highlight Reports from team managers to the board, and Checkpoint Reports from the board to the project manager
End Stage Reports to the board each week
Exception Reports for every checkpoint
Checkpoint Reports from team managers to the project manager, and Highlight Reports from the project manager to the board
items.explanation: Checkpoint Reports flow from team managers to the project manager, and the project manager consolidates progress into Highlight Reports for the board. Reversing the flow, using End Stage Reports weekly, or raising Exception Reports for every checkpoint is incorrect.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A team member raises a problem that could affect the stage's products. What should the project manager do in controlling a stage?
options: Capture the issue in the Issue Register, examine its impact, and decide or escalate as appropriate
Ignore it until the stage boundary
Record it as a lesson and take no further action
Ask the team member to resolve it without informing the project manager
items.explanation: Controlling a Stage includes capturing and examining issues and risks, assessing their impact, and deciding or escalating them. Deferring, merely logging a lesson, or leaving the issue unmanaged allows it to disrupt the stage.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A work package is running late but the stage is still forecast to remain within its overall tolerance. What should the project manager do?
options: Wait until the stage boundary to assess the delay
Take corrective action within the stage tolerances without escalating to the board
Immediately escalate an Exception Report to the board
Stop the stage and produce an Exception Plan
items.explanation: While a stage remains within its tolerances the project manager should take corrective action and continue, using management by exception. Escalation and Exception Plans are for forecast tolerance breaches, and waiting until the boundary leaves the delay unmanaged.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: The project manager wants to assess whether the stage will finish within its agreed tolerances. Which controlling a stage activity is this?
options: Deliver a work package to the customer
Prepare the Project Initiation Documentation
Review the stage status, comparing progress against the stage plan and tolerances
Authorize a work package for new work
items.explanation: Reviewing the stage status compares actual progress with the stage plan and tolerances to forecast the outcome. Work package authorization is a separate activity, delivery belongs to Managing Product Delivery, and the PID belongs to initiation.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: An issue is assessed and will cause the stage to exceed its cost tolerance. What should the project manager do?
options: Absorb the overspend by reducing quality checks
Change the stage plan and continue without informing the board
Record the issue and wait for the next Highlight Report
Escalate the issue and, if required, produce an Exception Plan for the board to authorize
items.explanation: When an issue or risk will breach a stage tolerance the project manager escalates it and, if asked, prepares an Exception Plan for board authorization. Reducing quality, hiding the deviation, or merely noting it denies the board its control.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A team manager receives a work package from the project manager. What should the team manager do FIRST in managing product delivery?
options: Accept the work package by confirming the products, tolerances, and reporting requirements can be met
Deliver the products immediately without checking the work package
Escalate the work package to the project board
Update the project plan and business case
items.explanation: Managing Product Delivery begins by accepting the work package and confirming that its products, tolerances, and reporting are understood and achievable. Delivering without agreement, escalating to the board, or updating higher-level documents is not the team manager's role here.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A team manager is executing a work package and must keep the project manager informed. What should the team manager provide?
options: An Exception Report to the board whenever a task slips
Checkpoint Reports at the frequency agreed in the work package
Highlight Reports to the project board
An End Project Report at the end of each work package
items.explanation: During execution the team manager provides Checkpoint Reports at the agreed frequency and escalates any forecast breach of the work package tolerances. Highlight Reports, End Project Reports, and direct board escalation are not part of Managing Product Delivery.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A team is building a product and must ensure it meets the quality criteria in its Product Description. Which action is correct?
options: Let the developer decide when the product is good enough
Skip quality checks to save time and cost
Perform the quality checks specified in the Product Description and record the results in the Quality Register
Wait until the project closes to check the product
items.explanation: Managing Product Delivery requires products to be checked against the quality criteria in their Product Descriptions, with results recorded in the Quality Register. Deferring, self-certifying, or skipping checks undermines the Quality theme.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: Within managing product delivery, what is the team manager responsible for?
options: Authorizing the project and approving the Business Case
Setting project-level tolerances for the board
Directing the project board's decisions
Accepting, executing, and delivering work packages and ensuring products meet their requirements
items.explanation: The team manager accepts, executes, and delivers work packages and ensures products meet their agreed requirements. Authorizing the project and setting tolerances are board responsibilities, and directing the board is not a project role.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A stage is nearing completion and the board needs assurance that it was completed as planned and that the next stage is justified. Which process covers this?
options: Managing a stage boundary, which reports stage end and plans the next stage
Controlling a stage, which monitors the current stage
Directing a project, which authorizes work
Closing a project, which brings the project to an end
items.explanation: Managing a Stage Boundary provides the board with the information to assess the completed stage and authorize the next one. Controlling a Stage is the ongoing monitoring, Directing a Project is the board's decisions, and Closing a Project is the final process.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: What should the project manager do as part of managing a stage boundary?
options: Hand over products and evaluate the project's benefits
Plan the next stage, update the project plan and business case, and report the stage end
Authorize the project and assemble the Project Brief
Accept and execute work packages
items.explanation: Managing a Stage Boundary includes planning the next stage, updating the project plan and Business Case, and producing an End Stage Report. Authorizing the project and Project Brief belong to earlier processes, and work packages and closure belong to other processes.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: A stage has breached its tolerance and the board asks the project manager to recover. Within managing a stage boundary, what is produced?
options: A Checkpoint Report for the current week
A Project Brief for a new project
An Exception Plan for the remainder of the stage or project, reviewed by the board
The original stage plan reissued unchanged
items.explanation: Managing a Stage Boundary produces an Exception Plan when a tolerance has been breached, replacing the plan for the remaining period for board approval. Reissuing the original plan, a Checkpoint Report, or a new Project Brief does not address recovery.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: The board needs to review the completed stage before authorizing the next one. Which product should the project manager provide?
options: A Highlight Report covering the final week
An End Project Report confirming closure
A Benefits Review Plan measuring benefits
An End Stage Report summarizing performance and the outlook for the next stage
items.explanation: The End Stage Report gives the board the information it needs to review the stage and decide on the next one at DP3. Highlight Reports are interim, End Project Reports close the project, and the Benefits Review Plan concerns benefit realization.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: The final products are ready and the project is ending. Which process brings the project to a controlled close?
options: Closing a project, which confirms acceptance, evaluates the project, and recommends closure
Managing a stage boundary, which plans the next stage
Controlling a stage, which monitors progress
Initiating a project, which establishes the baseline
items.explanation: Closing a Project confirms acceptance of the project's products, evaluates performance, and recommends closure to the board. Stage boundary, controlling a stage, and initiating a project serve earlier phases and do not close the project.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: Before the project can close, the customer must confirm that the final products are acceptable. What should the project manager do?
options: Ask the board to sign off without involving the customer
Obtain formal acceptance of the products and hand them over, recording acceptance in the relevant records
Assume acceptance because no one has complained
Hand over the products only after the project is closed
items.explanation: Closing a Project requires formal acceptance of the project's products from the customer and their handover to the operational environment. Assuming acceptance, handing over after closure, or bypassing the customer all fail the closure requirements.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: As part of closing a project the project manager reviews what went well and what could be improved. Which product should be produced?
options: A Checkpoint Report for the final week
A Work Package for the closing stage
A Lessons Report capturing lessons from the project for the organization
A new Project Brief for future work
items.explanation: Closing a Project produces a Lessons Report that captures the project's lessons for the organization, drawing on the Lessons Log. A Project Brief, Checkpoint Report, or Work Package is not the product used to share project lessons.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.stem: The board decides to stop the project before the products are complete. What should closing a project cover in this case?
options: Planned closure only, because products were not finished
An Exception Plan for the remaining work
A new stage boundary report
Premature closure, including the state of products, lessons, follow-on actions, and the updated Benefits Review Plan
items.explanation: Closing a Project covers both planned and premature closure, so when the board stops the project the project manager records the state of products, lessons, follow-on action recommendations, and updates the Benefits Review Plan. An Exception Plan or stage boundary report does not apply.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Applying PRINCE2 Processes

items.domain: Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment
items.stem: A project is low risk, small, and uses an existing, well-known solution. How should PRINCE2 be tailored?
options: Scale down the management products and combine roles, while still applying the principles
Apply every process and product at full weight regardless of size
Drop the principles to reduce effort
Use no documentation at all because the project is simple
items.explanation: Tailoring scales the method to the project's size, complexity, risk, and environment, simplifying products and combining roles while always applying the principles. Applying everything, dropping the principles, or abandoning documentation misapplies tailoring.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment

items.domain: Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment
items.stem: Where should the project manager record how PRINCE2 has been tailored for a particular project?
options: Verbally, to avoid adding paperwork
In the Project Initiation Documentation, so the tailoring decisions are baselined and visible
In the Daily Log, so they can be changed without notice
In the End Project Report, after delivery is complete
items.explanation: Tailoring decisions are recorded in the Project Initiation Documentation so the adapted method is agreed and baselined with the board. The Daily Log is for day-to-day notes, the End Project Report is retrospective, and verbal decisions cannot be assured.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment

items.domain: Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment
items.stem: On a small project one person will act as project manager and also provide project assurance. Why is this generally unsuitable?
options: Because project support must always be combined with assurance instead
Because the Executive must perform all assurance duties personally
Project assurance must be independent of the project manager, so combining the roles removes that independence
Because one person is not allowed to hold two PRINCE2 roles
items.explanation: Project Assurance monitors the project independently on behalf of the board, so combining it with the project manager role removes that independence. PRINCE2 allows roles to be combined when the project's size and risk permit, but not where independence is essential.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment

items.domain: Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment
items.stem: A project must comply with a regulatory framework that mandates specific approvals. How should PRINCE2 be tailored to this environment?
options: Ignore the regulatory approvals because PRINCE2 has its own controls
Apply PRINCE2 exactly as written even if it conflicts with the regulation
Replace PRINCE2 with the regulator's process entirely
Adapt the method so the project's processes and controls incorporate the mandatory approvals without losing the principles
items.explanation: Tailoring to the project environment means embedding legally required approvals into the method's processes and controls while retaining the principles. Ignoring the regulation, forcing a conflict, or abandoning PRINCE2 all fail to tailor appropriately.
items.reference: PRINCE2 Practitioner syllabus - Tailoring PRINCE2 to a Project Environment
